Indonesia
Consular help:Consular help will be provided by the Embassy of Bosnia and Herzegovina in Jakarta, Indonesia.
Visa required for the following traveling documentation for BH citizens (Visa shell be issued in Sarajevo):
Regular passport YES
Regular biometric passport YES
Service/Official biometric passport NO up to 30 days
Diplomatic biometric passport NO up to 30 days
Foreign nationals arriving in Indonesia are required to register through the following website: www.allindonesia.imigrasi.go.id, complete the required online form, and obtain a code that facilitates entry into the country.
Citizens of the Republic of Indonesia are required visas when entering, exiting or travelling through Bosnia and Herzegovina.Citizens of Indonesia, the holders of diplomatic and official passports, are exempted from the obligation to obtain a visa for entry, exit, transit and stay on the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina up to 90 days.
Holders of valid diplomatic and official passports who are assigned to work at the diplomatic and consular missions of Bosnia and Herzegovina in Jakarta, or at the diplomatic and consular missions of the Republic of Indonesia in Sarajevo, must, prior to entering the territory of the receiving State, obtain the appropriate entry visa issued by the competent diplomatic or consular mission of the receiving State. This requirement also applies to their family members, namely their spouse (husband/wife), unmarried and unemployed children up to 25 years of age, as well as dependent parents.
Security Conditions: The only region that remains problematic is Papua, located in the far eastern part of the country.
All citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina staying in private accommodation in the Republic of Indonesia (this does not apply to hotels, which register guests as part of their official duties) are required to register their stay with the competent “Rukun Tetangga” (RT) office responsible for the area in which they reside. Following registration, the RT office informs the competent police station of the registered stay. Therefore, citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina are not required to report directly to a police station, but only to the relevant RT office. The deadline for registration with the RT office varies from one locality to another; however, registration within 24 hours of arrival in the Republic of Indonesia is recommended.
Areas Requiring Increased Caution:
Papua: Visitors should exercise caution as separatist groups have carried out kidnappings of foreign nationals in remote areas. Travellers are advised to stay away from public gatherings, demonstrations, and protests.

Anak Krakatau (Little Krakatoa) and Other Volcanoes: Given that Indonesia is located within the so-called Pacific Ring of Fire, visits to volcanoes are popular tourist attractions but require caution. Safety conditions for visiting volcanoes can be checked through the State Volcanology Centre (PVMBG) website: https://vsi.esdm.go.id/. For further information, visitors may contact the Volcanology Centre in Bandung (+62 022 77 26 06 and +62 022 77 28 97) or in Yogyakarta (+62 0272 51 41 80).

Health Conditions: For the most serious medical cases, evacuation to Singapore is recommended.
Dengue fever occurs throughout the country, while malaria is present in certain regions. Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) did not result in any fatalities in Indonesia when it emerged.
Drugs: Drug-related offences are subject to very severe penalties, including the death penalty.
International Dialling Code: +62
